No. Neither of my prompts to the Figma agent mentioned dragging. I asked for the toolbar to be pinned inside the right edge of the 3D view, vertically centred, 12px in. So the frame shows one fixed position, with no drag handle, no snap targets, and no other placements. A static Figma frame can't show dragging anyway unless we add a visible grip and a note or extra frames for the other positions.

Vanilla OrcaSlicer's toolbars are also fixed; the user can't move them. I believe Unity's Scene view overlays can be dragged and docked to the view's edges, but I haven't verified that.

If you want it movable, this is the version I'd design:
- **Snap targets:** only the four edges of the 3D view, with no free-floating position. On the left or right edge the toolbar is vertical; on the top or bottom edge it switches to horizontal.
- **Placement on an edge:** centred by default. Optionally it could also snap to either end of the edge, which gives the corners.
- **Grab point:** a small grip at one end of the toolbar, so dragging it doesn't collide with clicking a tool.
- **Memory:** the chosen edge is saved per user and restored on the next launch.

My recommendation is to keep it fixed for now. It's one less thing to build and test. And the main reason to move a toolbar, getting it out of the way of the model, rarely comes up once the toolbar sits on the edge of the 3D view.

Do you want the draggable version added to the mockup, or should it stay fixed?

content.content:
# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, approval and verification requirements.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and authorization of consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.
# Handoff: the printer conversation panel on Home (wireframe 19b)

Status: approved for implementation by Kenneth on 2026-09-17. Nothing is built yet.

Today "+ Add printer" on Home opens a native modal dialog (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/`) that runs a fixed recognition script against OpenAI. This work deletes that dialog. Instead, Home's printers column turns into an agent conversation panel, the same shape as the Prepare-screen agent column, and the real agent handles both **adding** a printer and **changing** an existing one. Visual styling stays exactly as it is in the app today; only the layout, flow, copy and behaviour come from the wireframes.

Paths below are relative to the repo root. `J/` means `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.

---

## 1. Design sources (read these first)

Claude Design project `d981c5e2-20db-445f-9047-fa9e9a12522e`
(https://claude.ai/design/p/d981c5e2-20db-445f-9047-fa9e9a12522e). Read it through the DesignSync tool (`list_files` / `get_file`).

| File in the design project | What to read |
| --- | --- |
| `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` | Turn 19. Element `id="19b"`: the **Change** flow, a printer's conversation on Home. Element `id="19b-add"`: the **Add** flow, six panel states left to right. Also read turn 18 (`18a`–`18f`): 19b-add must carry all of 18's information, and 18e/18f describe "Set it up myself" and the no-agent state. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | The design's decision log. Read the sections "Printer conversation placement (turn 19)", "Add a printer (decided turn 18)", "Agent setup (decided turn 9–10)" and "Connect AI tools (turn 14)". Section 19 is marked "EXPLORATION, undecided"; Kenneth has since picked 19b, so this document overrides that label. |
| `support.js` | The runtime that renders `.dc.html` files. To view the wireframes, save both files into one folder and serve it over HTTP (for example `python3 -m http.server`), then open `wf.html#19b`. A `file://` URL does not work. Use a viewport of at least 1400 px. |

### How to read "pixel-perfect" here

The wireframes are deliberately **lo-fi**: Kalam sketch font, beige palette, and a 660 px frame in which the panel is 250 px wide. Do not copy their colours, fonts or pixel sizes. Match these exactly:

- the **structure and order** of every element in each panel state;
- the **relative emphasis**: which chip is filled, which value is muted, which text is red;
- the **copy**, word for word (quoted in section 3);
- the **behaviour** in the captions (section 3).

Take every colour, radius, font and control size from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: a value with no token gets a token and a guard first. Where the wireframe uses an element the app already has, reuse that element's current look:

| Wireframe class (in the `.dc.html` `<style>` block) | Existing app element to reuse |
| --- | --- |
| `.dlg-h` panel header | `J/AgentUI/src/components/ChatNavigation.tsx` |
| `.pin` pinned card, `.kv` rows | `J/AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx` and its `pinned-setup` band (`J/AgentUI/src/App.tsx`, near line 392) |
| `.abub` agent message, `.ubub` user message | `J/AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx` / `MarkdownMessage.tsx` |
| `.inp` composer, staged photo | `J/AgentUI/src/components/Composer.tsx`, `AttachmentChip.tsx` |
| `.pc` printer card with picture | New. Base it on Home's `J/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx` surface tokens. |
| `.opt` chip, `.opt.def` suggested chip, `.go` primary chip | New suggestion-chip row. Use existing button recipes (`--button-<recipe>-padding`) and the chip radius token. |

Panel width: the wireframe's 250 px is a proportion of a 660 px sketch, not a size. Use the existing Home printers-column token (`--printer-card-column-width`, 320 in `design-tokens.json` today) unless Kenneth says otherwise. The wireframe itself notes that the column is tight for picture cards, so check the ambiguous state (two picture cards) at that width.

---

## 2. Decisions already made (do not re-ask)

1. **Placement is 19b.** Home's printers column is replaced in place by the conversation panel. The projects gallery on the left stays visible. "‹ Printers" in the panel header returns to the printer list.
2. **Add is an open conversation with the real in-app agent**, not the old `PrinterSetupController` state machine and not the direct `OpenAIPrinterRecognition` call. Delete both.
3. **Change is in scope.** A printer's "Printer settings…" (the `…` menu on a Home printer card) opens this panel for that printer instead of OrcaSlicer's settings window.
4. **"Printer settings…" in the Prepare header's printer menu** (`J/Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp`, around line 105) also goes to Home and opens the same panel for the current printer.
5. **"Set it up myself"** in the panel header:
   - Add flow: opens OrcaSlicer's ConfigWizard printer page, unchanged. This is what `run_manual_setup` in `J/PrinterSetup/PrinterSetupLauncher.cpp` does today; keep that behaviour when you delete the file.
   - Change flow: opens OrcaSlicer's existing printer settings window, which is what "Printer settings…" did before (`Printers::open_named_printer_settings` → `SetupCommands::open_settings_tab(TYPE_PRINTER)`).
6. **Delete the old native dialog** and its tests (see section 5).
7. **No agent set up:** the panel shows the same agent-setup page and flow the old dialog embedded: a throwaway `AgentWebView` loaded with `?embedded=1`. When setup finishes, the panel switches to the conversation.
8. **An external AI tool is connected instead of an in-app agent** (the "Connect an AI tool" / MCP path, where the model runs in Claude Code, Cursor and so on): the Home panel has no in-app agent to talk to, so it shows the agent-setup page, the same as decision 7.
9. **Leave out the re-slice claim.** The 19b Change wireframe's agent reply says "Your two projects on this printer will re-slice with it next time you open them." Nothing implements that, so the agent must not say it.

---

## 3. Screen specification

### 3.1 Panel anatomy (every state)

From top to bottom:

1. **Header**:
   - left: `‹` then the label **"Printers"** (the label names where ‹ leads, not the current printer);
   - right: the link **"Set it up myself"**.
   - There is no close ×; ‹ is the way out.
2. **Pinned card**:
   - a small uppercase caption, **"NEW PRINTER"** (Add) or **"PRINTER"** (Change);
   - four label/value rows: **Printer · Nozzle · Plate · Filament**.
   - Each value has one of four styles:
     - *empty*: an em dash `—` in the most muted text colour;
     - *settled*: normal weight-600 text;
     - *assumed*: regular-weight secondary text with the suffix ` · assumed`;
     - *changed*: accent/red text with the suffix ` · changed`.
   - The Filament value can include a colour swatch (see the "Use this" state).

- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from

   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.

content.content:
## Runtime application in the native app

The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.

1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
     fonts.
   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:
   - `StateColor::SetColorOverrides` maps OrcaSlicer's brand and surface
     literals (teal family, grays, whites, text grays) to semantic tokens before
     OrcaSlicer's own dark-mode remap runs. Every widget built on `StateColor`
     switches at once.
   - `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces` rewrites the teal in the SVG icon set to
     the action color at load time, and the monochrome brand mark to the text
     color.
   - The ImGui panels, the canvas selection rectangle, and the About dialog
     are left alone in source: those surfaces are slated to be hidden or
     replaced, so editing them would be divergence with no lasting value.
   - The mapping table in `BrandPalette.cpp` is the reviewed teal-to-purple
     decision. Extend it there; never add a purple literal to an OrcaSlicer file.
   - Widgets that paint the teal without going through `StateColor` (hyperlinks,
     the settings tab underline, notification accents, Bambu-only dialogs) are
     deliberately left teal; the cost of editing them in busy upstream files
     outweighs surfaces JusPrin rarely or never shows.
3. **Identity** comes from two data-only mechanisms:
   - `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds the splash, About and horizontal
     lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icons under
     OrcaSlicer's own asset names. `Slic3r::var()` checks that directory
     first, so no logo call site is edited. See the README there.
   - `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` builds `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`
     from upstream's `.po` files with the product name substituted, plus an
     English catalog for the source strings, so every language reads "JusPrin"
     without touching a string or macro in upstream code. Attribution strings
     in About are excluded by the script.
   - The generic printer profiles' plate texture,
     `resources/profiles/Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg`, is overwritten
     with the JusPrin lockup; the file name stays because five profiles
     reference it.

`tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` fails the build if a token edit breaks the
contrast rules above or leaves a token in one mode without its counterpart in
the other. The same test guards the radius, spacing, and type scales: the
`dimension.radius`, `dimension.space`, and `typography.roles` tables must match
the values in this document exactly, `typography.code` must stay a single
12/16 role, every component radius must be one of the scale values, and every
button recipe must name a type role rather than a raw size.

Known gaps, all deliberate: ImGui panels and canvas notifications keep the
teal accent; the first-run setup wizard (an OrcaSlicer HTML page) is
Orca-branded until JusPrin's own onboarding replaces it; the About dialog
links to the OrcaSlicer website; vendor printer profiles other than the
generic ones keep their own plate textures; dark mode and the Preview canvas
were not visually verified.

## Design handoff requirements

Every high-fidelity product frame must:

1. Include paired light and dark versions using the same semantic token names.
2. State the mode, viewport, component variants, keyboard focus, and any deliberate exception.
3. Use DIP, native density, and the standard radius scale.
4. Use HarmonyOS Sans SC for product UI, and monospace only for code (Figma's Code style uses Roboto Mono as a stand-in for the system font).
5. Show normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focus, error, warning, and success states as applicable.
6. Test long filenames, localized labels, dense settings, empty states, and narrow windows.
7. Use the original logo and existing functional icon system.
8. Label and justify any value that is not in the token files.

The POC decks, rendered examples, horizontal lockup PNG, and generation sources remain available for visual-reference work through [POC reference](poc-reference.md). They are not runtime dependencies.
## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden

## Runtime application in the native app

The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.

1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
     fonts.
   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:
   - `StateColor::SetColorOverrides` maps OrcaSlicer's brand and surface
     literals (teal family, grays, whites, text grays) to semantic tokens before
     OrcaSlicer's own dark-mode remap runs. Every widget built on `StateColor`
     switches at once.
   - `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces` rewrites the teal in the SVG icon set to
     the action color at load time, and the monochrome brand mark to the text
     color.
   - The ImGui panels, the canvas selection rectangle, and the About dialog
     are left alone in source: those surfaces are slated to be hidden or
     replaced, so editing them would be divergence with no lasting value.
   - The mapping table in `BrandPalette.cpp` is the reviewed teal-to-purple
     decision. Extend it there; never add a purple literal to an OrcaSlicer file.
   - Widgets that paint the teal without going through `StateColor` (hyperlinks,
     the settings tab underline, notification accents, Bambu-only dialogs) are
     deliberately left teal; the cost of editing them in busy upstream files
     outweighs surfaces JusPrin rarely or never shows.
3. **Identity** comes from two data-only mechanisms:
   - `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds the splash, About and horizontal
     lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icons under
     OrcaSlicer's own asset names. `Slic3r::var()` checks that directory
     first, so no logo call site is edited. See the README there.
   - `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` builds `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`
     from upstream's `.po` files with the product name substituted, plus an
     English catalog for the source strings, so every language reads "JusPrin"
     without touching a string or macro in upstream code. Attribution strings
     in About are excluded by the script.
   - The generic printer profiles' plate texture,
     `resources/profiles/Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg`, is overwritten
     with the JusPrin lockup; the file name stays because five profiles
     reference it.

`tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` fails the build if a token edit breaks the
contrast rules above or leaves a token in one mode without its counterpart in
the other. The same test guards the radius, spacing, and type scales: the
`dimension.radius`, `dimension.space`, and `typography.roles` tables must match
the values in this document exactly, `typography.code` must stay a single
12/16 role, every component radius must be one of the scale values, and every
button recipe must name a type role rather than a raw size.

teal accent; the first-run setup wizard (an OrcaSlicer HTML page) is
Orca-branded until JusPrin's own onboarding replaces it; the About dialog
links to the OrcaSlicer website; vendor printer profiles other than the
generic ones keep their own plate textures; dark mode and the Preview canvas
were not visually verified.

## Design handoff requirements

Every high-fidelity product frame must:

1. Include paired light and dark versions using the same semantic token names.
2. State the mode, viewport, component variants, keyboard focus, and any deliberate exception.
3. Use DIP, native density, and the standard radius scale.
4. Use HarmonyOS Sans SC for product UI, and monospace only for code (Figma's Code style uses Roboto Mono as a stand-in for the system font).
5. Show normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focus, error, warning, and success states as applicable.
6. Test long filenames, localized labels, dense settings, empty states, and narrow windows.
7. Use the original logo and existing functional icon system.
8. Label and justify any value that is not in the token files.

The POC decks, rendered examples, horizontal lockup PNG, and generation sources remain available for visual-reference work through [POC reference](poc-reference.md). They are not runtime dependencies.

# Handoff: 3D selection brackets and the viewport tool strip (Prepare canvas)

Status: direction approved by Kenneth on 2026-09-18. Nothing is built yet. Section 7 lists the questions that still need his answer; each one has a recommended default so the work does not stall.

The Prepare screen's 3D view (the OpenGL canvas where the user arranges models on the plate) needs two things:

1. **A restyled selection indicator.** Keep OrcaSlicer's approach, 3D corner brackets on the selected object's bounding box, but make it quieter and on-brand.
2. **A vertical object-tool strip** (Move, Rotate, Scale, Duplicate, More) fixed inside the right edge of the 3D view.

The shell currently hides every OrcaSlicer toolbar on this canvas, so today there is **no on-screen way to move, rotate or scale an object**. The tool strip fills that gap.

Paths are relative to the repo root. `J/` means `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Line numbers were measured on `jusprin-newui` at `35eb1b4a59`; re-find them by symbol name if they have drifted.

Read before starting:

- `AGENTS.md`.
- `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. This work needs small seams in `GLCanvas3D.cpp` and `Selection.cpp`, which are OrcaSlicer-owned files.
- "Writing UI code" and "Runtime application in the native app" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`.

---

## 1. Design source

Figma file "JusPrin v2", Main Page, frame **`maker-at-work-tools-attach`** (node `36-2`):
https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=36-2

Layers that matter, all under `workspace-container › center-column › center-viewport`:

| Layer | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `model-and-controls › model-selection-wrapper › 3d-model-render` | A static picture standing in for the live 3D view (568×712). |
| `model-and-controls › model-selection-wrapper › selection-3d-brackets` | Vector corner brackets drawn over the picture. They are approximate, placed by eye; treat them as a style reference, not geometry. |
| `viewport-toolbar` | The tool strip. Its values are copied into section 3.2, so you do not need Figma access to build it. |

The Figma MCP connection on this account is a View seat limited to about 6 reads a month, so prefer the values below over reading Figma. The design was reached in three steps, and knowing them explains the constraints:

1. It started with a flat 2D dashed rectangle around the object and the tool strip docked to that rectangle.
2. Kenneth rejected that on 2026-09-18. No 3D slicer, CAD or game-engine editor surveyed uses a flat screen rectangle; they use 3D boxes, outlines or tints. A toolbar attached to the selection would also jump around whenever the camera orbits.
3. The frame was then redrawn in the OrcaSlicer direction.

---

## 2. Decisions already made (do not re-ask)

1. **The selection indicator is drawn in 3D**, as corner brackets on the selection's world-space bounding box, the mechanism OrcaSlicer already uses. No 2D screen-space rectangle and no silhouette-to-screen box.
2. **The tool strip is fixed to the 3D view, not to the selection.** It does not follow the object, the camera, or zoom.
3. **The tool strip cannot be dragged.** Kenneth was offered a draggable version that snaps to the view's edges and chose to keep it fixed for now.
4. **The tools are Move, Rotate, Scale, Duplicate and More**, in that order, with a divider before More.
5. **Everything else on the Prepare screen stays as it is**: top bar, plates and objects sidebar, agent chat column, and the Slice menu.

---

## 3. Specification

### 3.1 Selection brackets

Today the brackets are drawn by `Selection::render` → `Selection::render_bounding_box` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Selection.cpp:2001`, `:2619`):

- white (yellow in the assemble view);
- each arm 20% of the box edge, three arms per corner, eight corners;
- a 1.5 px thick-line shader on core OpenGL profiles, or `glLineWidth(2 × scale)` on compatibility profiles;
- depth-tested (`glEnable(GL_DEPTH_TEST)` at `:2741`), so arms behind the model are already hidden by the model;
- down-arrows under the bottom corners when the object is not resting on the bed (`auto_drop`).

Change only what the design changes:

| Property | Now | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Colour | `ColorRGB::WHITE()` hard-coded at `Selection.cpp:2011` | the token `semantic.<mode>.action.primary` (Figma `action/primary`), read through `ShellTheme` for the current light/dark mode |
| Arm length | 20% of each edge | unchanged (the design asks for 15–20%) |
| Line width | 1.5 px (core) / 2 px × scale (compatibility) | unchanged |
| Hidden arms | removed by the depth test | unchanged. Do not add hidden-corner culling; the depth test already gives the "light cage" look |
| Down-arrows when floating | shown | unchanged |
| Assemble-view colour (yellow) | yellow | unchanged; that view is out of scope |

Figma draws round line caps. The thick-line shader draws square ends, and 1.5 px lines show no visible difference, so **do not change the shader**.

Mesh tint: a selected object is brightened by +0.25 HSL lightness (`GLVolume::set_render_color`, `src/slic3r/GUI/3DScene.cpp:325`). Leave it; the design does not change it.

### 3.2 Tool strip

Geometry, measured in the Figma frame and matched to `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`:

| Part | Figma value | Token to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Position | inside the 3D view, right edge inset 12, vertically centred on the view | spacing 12 is on the layout scale (`ShellTheme::metrics().space_3`) |
| Strip layout | vertical; padding 6; gap 4 between buttons | 4 is on the scale. **6 is not on the spacing scale**; see question Q3 |
| Strip surface | fill `surface/raised`, 1 px inside stroke `border/subtle`, corner radius 8, shadow `Elevation/Medium` | `semantic.*.surface.raised`, `semantic.*.border.subtle`, `dimension.radius.container` (8), `elevation.medium` |
| Button | 28×28, radius 4 | **Conflict:** the existing icon-button token is 26×26 with a 16 px icon and radius 4 (`component.button.icon`). See Q3 |
| Icon | 14×14, stroke icons | **Conflict:** `component.icon.sizes` is [16, 20, 24]; 14 is not on it. See Q3 |
| Idle button | no fill; icon `text/secondary` | `semantic.*.text.secondary` |
| Hover | not drawn in Figma | `semantic.*.surface.selected` fill (the icon-button recipe's hover); confirm against `ShellRecipes` |
| Active tool | fill `action/primary`, icon `action/on-primary` | `semantic.*.action.primary`, `semantic.*.text.onAction` |
| Disabled | not drawn | icon `semantic.*.action.disabledText`, no hover |
| Divider before More | 20 px line, 1 px, `border/subtle` | `semantic.*.border.subtle` |

Every colour, radius and size comes through `ShellTheme` (`J/Shell/ShellTheme.hpp`: `palette(dark)`, `metrics()`). Follow "Writing UI code" rule 2: a value with no token gets a token and a guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` first. Do not type 28, 14 or 6.

Icons: Figma uses Lucide-style stroke icons (Lucide names: `move`, `rotate-cw`, `maximize-2`, `copy`, `ellipsis`). Add them as SVGs to `resources/jusprin/ui/icons/`, beside `plus.svg`, `close.svg` and `chevron-left.svg`, in the same `currentColor` format. Tint them at load time. OrcaSlicer's `toolbar_move.svg` / `toolbar_rotate.svg` / `toolbar_scale.svg` are a different visual family; do not reuse them.

Behaviour of each button:

| Button | Action | Existing entry point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | open the Move tool; click again to close it | `CanvasPresentationController::activate_move()` (`J/CanvasPresentationController.cpp:23`), which calls `GLGizmosManager::open_gizmo(EType::Move)` |
| Rotate | open the Rotate tool; click again to close it | `activate_rotate()` |
| Scale | open the Scale tool; click again to close it | add `activate_scale()` beside the other two (fork-owned file) |
| Duplicate | add one copy of the selected object | `Plater::increase_instances(1)` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.hpp:521`); see Q4 |
| More | open the object's right-click menu, anchored to the button's left edge | `Plater::object_menu()` (`Plater.hpp:945`), shown with `PopupMenu` on the canvas |

Toggle semantics: `activate()` returns early when the requested tool is already open (`CanvasPresentationController.cpp:38`), but `open_gizmo` itself closes a tool that is already open. Clicking the active button must close the tool, so change `activate()` to toggle, or add a separate close call. Do not leave a click on the active button as a silent no-op.

2. Kenneth rejected that on 2026-09-18. No 3D slicer, CAD or game-engine editor surveyed uses a flat screen rectangle; they use 3D boxes, outlines or tints. A toolbar attached to the selection would also jump around whenever the camera orbits.
3. The frame was then redrawn in the OrcaSlicer direction.

---

## 2. Decisions already made (do not re-ask)

1. **The selection indicator is drawn in 3D**, as corner brackets on the selection's world-space bounding box, the mechanism OrcaSlicer already uses. No 2D screen-space rectangle and no silhouette-to-screen box.
2. **The tool strip is fixed to the 3D view, not to the selection.** It does not follow the object, the camera, or zoom.
3. **The tool strip cannot be dragged.** Kenneth was offered a draggable version that snaps to the view's edges and chose to keep it fixed for now.
4. **The tools are Move, Rotate, Scale, Duplicate and More**, in that order, with a divider before More.
5. **Everything else on the Prepare screen stays as it is**: top bar, plates and objects sidebar, agent chat column, and the Slice menu.

---

## 3. Specification

### 3.1 Selection brackets

Today the brackets are drawn by `Selection::render` → `Selection::render_bounding_box` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Selection.cpp:2001`, `:2619`):

- white (yellow in the assemble view);
- each arm 20% of the box edge, three arms per corner, eight corners;
- a 1.5 px thick-line shader on core OpenGL profiles, or `glLineWidth(2 × scale)` on compatibility profiles;
- depth-tested (`glEnable(GL_DEPTH_TEST)` at `:2741`), so arms behind the model are already hidden by the model;
- down-arrows under the bottom corners when the object is not resting on the bed (`auto_drop`).

Change only what the design changes:

| Property | Now | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Colour | `ColorRGB::WHITE()` hard-coded at `Selection.cpp:2011` | the token `semantic.<mode>.action.primary` (Figma `action/primary`), read through `ShellTheme` for the current light/dark mode |
| Arm length | 20% of each edge | unchanged (the design asks for 15–20%) |
| Line width | 1.5 px (core) / 2 px × scale (compatibility) | unchanged |
| Hidden arms | removed by the depth test | unchanged. Do not add hidden-corner culling; the depth test already gives the "light cage" look |
| Down-arrows when floating | shown | unchanged |
| Assemble-view colour (yellow) | yellow | unchanged; that view is out of scope |

Figma draws round line caps. The thick-line shader draws square ends, and 1.5 px lines show no visible difference, so **do not change the shader**.

Mesh tint: a selected object is brightened by +0.25 HSL lightness (`GLVolume::set_render_color`, `src/slic3r/GUI/3DScene.cpp:325`). Leave it; the design does not change it.

### 3.2 Tool strip

Geometry, measured in the Figma frame and matched to `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`:

| Part | Figma value | Token to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Position | inside the 3D view, right edge inset 12, vertically centred on the view | spacing 12 is on the layout scale (`ShellTheme::metrics().space_3`) |
| Strip layout | vertical; padding 6; gap 4 between buttons | 4 is on the scale. **6 is not on the spacing scale**; see question Q3 |
| Strip surface | fill `surface/raised`, 1 px inside stroke `border/subtle`, corner radius 8, shadow `Elevation/Medium` | `semantic.*.surface.raised`, `semantic.*.border.subtle`, `dimension.radius.container` (8), `elevation.medium` |
| Button | 28×28, radius 4 | **Conflict:** the existing icon-button token is 26×26 with a 16 px icon and radius 4 (`component.button.icon`). See Q3 |
| Icon | 14×14, stroke icons | **Conflict:** `component.icon.sizes` is [16, 20, 24]; 14 is not on it. See Q3 |
| Idle button | no fill; icon `text/secondary` | `semantic.*.text.secondary` |
| Hover | not drawn in Figma | `semantic.*.surface.selected` fill (the icon-button recipe's hover); confirm against `ShellRecipes` |
| Active tool | fill `action/primary`, icon `action/on-primary` | `semantic.*.action.primary`, `semantic.*.text.onAction` |
| Disabled | not drawn | icon `semantic.*.action.disabledText`, no hover |
| Divider before More | 20 px line, 1 px, `border/subtle` | `semantic.*.border.subtle` |

Every colour, radius and size comes through `ShellTheme` (`J/Shell/ShellTheme.hpp`: `palette(dark)`, `metrics()`). Follow "Writing UI code" rule 2: a value with no token gets a token and a guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` first. Do not type 28, 14 or 6.

Icons: Figma uses Lucide-style stroke icons (Lucide names: `move`, `rotate-cw`, `maximize-2`, `copy`, `ellipsis`). Add them as SVGs to `resources/jusprin/ui/icons/`, beside `plus.svg`, `close.svg` and `chevron-left.svg`, in the same `currentColor` format. Tint them at load time. OrcaSlicer's `toolbar_move.svg` / `toolbar_rotate.svg` / `toolbar_scale.svg` are a different visual family; do not reuse them.

Behaviour of each button:

| Button | Action | Existing entry point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | open the Move tool; click again to close it | `CanvasPresentationController::activate_move()` (`J/CanvasPresentationController.cpp:23`), which calls `GLGizmosManager::open_gizmo(EType::Move)` |
| Rotate | open the Rotate tool; click again to close it | `activate_rotate()` |
| Scale | open the Scale tool; click again to close it | add `activate_scale()` beside the other two (fork-owned file) |
| Duplicate | add one copy of the selected object | `Plater::increase_instances(1)` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.hpp:521`); see Q4 |
| More | open the object's right-click menu, anchored to the button's left edge | `Plater::object_menu()` (`Plater.hpp:945`), shown with `PopupMenu` on the canvas |

Toggle semantics: `activate()` returns early when the requested tool is already open (`CanvasPresentationController.cpp:38`), but `open_gizmo` itself closes a tool that is already open. Clicking the active button must close the tool, so change `activate()` to toggle, or add a separate close call. Do not leave a click on the active button as a silent no-op.

The active state must be **read, not remembered**: take `GLGizmosManager::get_current_type()` each frame. Tools can also open through their keyboard shortcuts (`m_shortcut_key` in `GLGizmoMove.cpp:64`, `GLGizmoRotate.cpp:558`, `GLGizmoScale.cpp:138`), through the Agent, or close when the selection changes, and the highlight must follow all of those.

Tooltips: the tool name plus its shortcut. Verify the actual keys in the running app before writing them; do not copy them from memory or from this document.

Visibility: see Q1 and Q2.

---

## 4. What the code does today

- `J/CanvasPresentationController` hides every OrcaSlicer overlay on the Prepare canvas through `GLCanvas3D::set_legacy_overlays_hidden(true)` (`GLCanvas3D.cpp:1809`). `J/Shell/ShellController.cpp:258-269` attaches it.
  - With overlays hidden, `_render_overlays()` is skipped entirely (`GLCanvas3D.cpp:2148`): the main toolbar, the gizmo toolbar, the gizmo input panels, labels and the navigator.
  - The active gizmo's 3D handles still draw (`_render_current_gizmo`), and the picker input is off.
- The selection brackets are **not** an overlay. `_render_selection` (`GLCanvas3D.cpp:8297`) draws them whenever **no gizmo is open**, and they still render today, in white.
- `activate_move()` and `activate_rotate()` exist but nothing calls them.
- No fork code draws anything inside the canvas. No ImGui is used under `J/`, and no wx child window sits over the canvas.
- `ShellTheme` has the palette fields the strip needs: `surface_raised`, `border_subtle`, `action_primary*`, `surface_selected`. It has no canvas-specific tokens.

---

## 5. Implementation guidance

### 5.1 Drawing the tool strip: recommended approach

Draw the strip **inside the canvas's own render pass, with ImGui**, the way every OrcaSlicer canvas control is drawn. Feed it colours, radii and sizes from `ShellTheme`. This is my recommendation, not a verified result: prove it with a small spike before building the rest.

- **Why not a native wx child window over the canvas:** a child window laid over an OpenGL canvas behaves differently on each platform (transparency, rounded corners, shadows outside the window's bounds, flicker on GTK), and the strip needs rounded corners and a shadow. ImGui draws in the same GL frame, so none of that arises, and OrcaSlicer's own canvas controls prove it works on all three platforms.
- **The seam:** `_render_overlays()` does not run while legacy overlays are hidden, so the fork needs one additive hook in `GLCanvas3D`. For example, a `std::function<void()>` member that `render()` calls after the `if (!m_legacy_overlays_hidden) _render_overlays();` line, plus a public setter. `J/CanvasPresentationController` sets it on attach and clears it on detach. Keep the hook product-neutral: it knows nothing about toolbars.
- **Mouse input:** ImGui windows already take mouse priority over the canvas through `ImGuiWrapper` and the canvas's `want_mouse` checks. Verify that a click on the strip neither deselects the object nor starts a rectangle selection.
- **Redraws:** the canvas redraws on demand. Call `set_as_dirty()` and `request_extra_frame()` after anything that changes the strip (see how `activate()` does it).
- **Code location:** the strip's layout and drawing go in a new fork-owned file under `J/` (for example `J/Canvas/ViewportToolStrip.{hpp,cpp}`). It holds everything product-specific: order, icons, token lookups, button actions.

### 5.2 Colouring the brackets

The bracket colour is a literal in an upstream file. Follow the pattern `BrandPalette.cpp` already uses for `StateColor` and `BitmapCache`:

1. Add a small, product-neutral, optional override to `Selection`, such as a static `set_bounding_box_color_override(std::optional<ColorRGB>)`, which `render()` uses in place of `WHITE()` when set.
2. Install it from `J/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` for each appearance mode.

That keeps OrcaSlicer's stock behaviour when the fork is off and avoids editing the colour call site's logic.

### 5.3 Fork-stewardship evidence (required)

For every OrcaSlicer-owned line touched (`GLCanvas3D.{hpp,cpp}`, `Selection.{hpp,cpp}`), record in the pull request what `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` "Before you finish" requires:

- the `git merge-tree` rebase simulation, with both endpoint commits named;
- an account of any upstream line deleted or rewritten (the target is zero);
- a statement of what the fork now owns.

`GLCanvas3D.cpp` is one of the busiest files the fork touches, so keep the hook to a few lines.

---

## 6. Verification

**Automated tests** (Catch2, in `tests/jusprin/`):

- `activate()` toggles: opening, re-clicking and switching tools each leave `get_current_type()` correct.
- The strip's hit-testing and layout: button rectangles for a given canvas size, the 12 px inset, vertical centring.
- Token lookups: every strip value resolves from `ShellTheme`. Extend `test_brand_tokens.cpp` for any new token.
- Run `brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests` and `jusprin_tests`.

**The real app:** run `tests/shell/shell_integration_harness` in `--manual` mode with a fixture project (build steps in `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`, around line 849). Its `write_screen_capture` saves PNGs. The MCP `view_render` tool renders through the thumbnail path and does **not** show overlays or brackets, so it is not evidence here. Check each of these:

1. Select an object: purple brackets appear and the strip shows no active tool.
2. Click Move: the Move handles appear and the button highlights. Drag an object and confirm the move applies and undoes.
3. Repeat for Rotate and Scale.
4. Click the active button: the tool closes.
5. Open a tool with its keyboard shortcut: the strip highlight follows.
6. Duplicate adds exactly one copy, and one undo removes it.
7. More opens the object menu next to the button.
8. Clicking the strip never changes the selection or starts a drag-select.
9. Orbit, pan and zoom: the strip stays put and the brackets follow the object.
10. Dark mode: the strip and the brackets use the dark tokens.
11. Narrow window: the strip never overlaps the right-hand chat column.

The design system notes that dark mode and the Preview canvas were never visually verified in this app, so look at dark mode yourself; do not infer it.

**Platforms:** the strip is drawn by the canvas, so check macOS and Windows at least. The Windows test VM is described in the team's notes; ask Kenneth if you need access.

---

## 7. Open questions for Kenneth (with defaults)

- **Q1. Brackets while a tool is open.** The Figma frame shows the brackets and an active Move button at the same time, with no Move handles. OrcaSlicer hides the brackets whenever a tool is open (`_render_selection`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp:8305`) and shows the tool's handles instead. **Default: keep OrcaSlicer's behaviour**, so an open tool shows its handles and no brackets. Treat the Figma frame as two states merged into one picture.
- **Q2. Strip with nothing selected.** Figma shows only the selected state. **Default: hide the strip when the selection is empty.** The alternative is to show it with all buttons disabled so users can discover it.
- **Q3. Button, icon and padding sizes.** Figma uses 28 px buttons, 14 px icons and 6 px padding. The token file's icon button is 26 px with a 16 px icon, and 6 is not on the spacing scale. **Default: use the existing `component.button.icon` token (26 / 16 / radius 4) and padding 4**, which keeps the icon system consistent. That strip is 36 px wide instead of 40. If Kenneth prefers Figma's sizes, add tokens and guards first.
- **Q4. What Duplicate does.** **Default: `Plater::increase_instances(1)`**: one click, one extra copy, placed by OrcaSlicer's own logic, undoable. The alternative, `Plater::clone_selection()`, opens a modal dialog asking how many copies.
- **Q5. The purple on dark 3D scenes.** `action.primary` was chosen for UI surfaces, not for thin lines over a grey 3D scene. **Default: use it, then check contrast in both modes in the running app.** If it fails, raise it with Kenneth; do not invent a new colour.

---

## 8. Out of scope

- Dragging or snapping the strip (decision 3).
- The Preview canvas and the assemble view.
- Restyling the gizmos' own 3D handles or their numeric input panels. The input panels stay hidden with the other legacy overlays; if Kenneth wants numeric entry for Move, Rotate or Scale, that is a separate design.
- The mesh tint and the optional outline shader (`show_outline`).

I wrote the handoff doc at [viewport-selection-toolbar-handoff.md](agent-docs/jusprin/viewport-selection-toolbar-handoff.md) and copied it to `C:\Users\guitest\Downloads\` on `jusprin-win-test`. The copy on the VM is the same size as the local file (16,718 bytes). The doc isn't committed; it sits untracked next to the printer-panel handoff.

Since the coding agent can read Figma, the doc points to the `maker-at-work-tools-attach` frame and its `viewport-toolbar` layer instead of describing the visuals. It covers what Figma can't show:

- **Decisions already made:** selection is shown with 3D brackets, the toolbar is fixed to the 3D view, and it isn't draggable.
- **Where the Figma values disagree with the token file:** Figma's 28 px buttons, 14 px icons and 6 px padding aren't in the token file, which has a 26 px icon button with 16 px icons.
- **What each button does:**
  - Move, Rotate and Scale open OrcaSlicer's existing tools. The fork already has unused `activate_move()` and `activate_rotate()` functions; Scale needs one added.
  - Duplicate adds one copy of the object.
  - More opens the object's right-click menu.
  - The highlighted button is read from whichever tool is actually open, so it stays correct when a tool is opened by keyboard shortcut or by the Agent.
- **Where the code goes:** the toolbar is drawn inside the 3D canvas using OrcaSlicer's own canvas UI library (ImGui), through one small hook in `GLCanvas3D`. The bracket colour becomes the brand purple through a small optional override in `Selection`, the same way the brand palette already recolours other OrcaSlicer widgets. The fork-stewardship evidence those upstream edits need is listed too.
- **How to verify it**, as an 11-item checklist in the running app. The Agent's `view_render` tool doesn't show overlays, so it can't serve as evidence here.

Two findings from the code change the picture:

- **Today there's no on-screen way to move, rotate or scale an object on the Prepare screen.** The shell hides all of OrcaSlicer's canvas toolbars, so this toolbar fills a real gap.
- **The Figma frame shows two states merged into one.** It has the brackets visible while Move is highlighted, but OrcaSlicer hides the brackets whenever a tool is open and shows that tool's handles instead.

Five questions are left for you. Each has a default in the doc, so the implementer won't get stuck:

1. **Brackets while a tool is open.** Default: keep OrcaSlicer's behaviour, so an open tool shows its handles and no brackets.
2. **Toolbar with nothing selected.** Default: hide it.
3. **Button and icon sizes.** Default: use the existing 26 px / 16 px icon-button token, which makes the strip 34 px wide instead of Figma's 40.
4. **What Duplicate does.** Default: add one copy directly. The alternative is OrcaSlicer's clone dialog, which asks how many copies.
5. **Bracket colour.** Default: use the brand purple (`action.primary`), then check it stays visible against the grey 3D scene in both light and dark mode.
